findings.reason: Confirmed on the sources, at the cited lines. ClassicalGroups README line 303 reads 'equivalently, the specialization of the abstract Weyl dimension formula `∏_{α > 0} ⟨λ + ρ, α⟩ / ⟨ρ, α⟩` from [`../RootSystems`](../RootSystems/README.md)', and lines 294-295 read 'The general Weyl character formula for `SLₙ`, `Spₙ`, `SOₙ` follows from [`../RootSystems`](../RootSystems/README.md)'s Weyl-group sum over the appropriate root system.' RootSystems' scope boundary at lines 45-51 reads 'The weight and root lattices, the coweight and coroot lattices, the fundamental weights, dominant integral weights, and `ρ` - the lattice apparatus that the Weyl character and dimension formulas run on - are **not** built here; they belong to [the highest-weight roadmap](../LieHighestWeight/README.md)'. The boundary names the Weyl character and dimension formulas explicitly as what the excluded apparatus runs on, so ClassicalGroups cites RootSystems for precisely the two things RootSystems disclaims, and a worker building Layers 4-5 would look there for ρ and not find it. Medium severity is right: this misdirects construction rather than merely reading badly. The proposed fix is also well judged, and I would keep it as written: the Layer 4 citation is half correct, since the Weyl-group sum really is indexed by the root system's Weyl group, which RootSystems does own, and the fix splits the sentence on exactly that line rather than moving the whole citation. I applied the standard that rejected RT-AUDIT-22/1 — whether the format already carries the truth in another field — and it does not here: the prose is the only statement of ownership, and it is wrong.

Confirmed, with every quantitative detail reproduced. Five extractions route to RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure with exactly the item counts the finding gives — PAPER-HE-18 21, PAPER-HE-21 28, PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-ZHOU-26 22, PAPER-LE-LEHUNG-LEVIN-ETAL-23 26, PAPER-ZHU-17 1 — while PAPER-KISIN-ZHOU-25 routes 8 items to the separate id RootSystemsDominancePartII with the reason 'Extend the existing proposed owner for integral dominance by the reusable finite diagram-folding and invariant-step proof.' The string 'RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure' does not occur anywhere in PAPER-KISIN-ZHOU-25's record, and its coalescence block is null. PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-ZHOU-26 does record the overlap, verbatim: 'The Kisin–Zhou candidate RootSystemsDominancePartII overlaps this earlier direction: consolidate its dominant-coroot/Stembridge lane into this candidate at design intake'. So the duplication is real, is known in exactly one of the six records, and is invisible from the KZ-25 side. That is the distinction that makes this more than a bookkeeping remark: a design job reading PAPER-KISIN-ZHOU-25 alone would build a second roadmap in a direction already planned, which section 15 forbids. Medium severity is right, and the proposed fix — consolidate onto the id five extractions share, keep KZ-25's 8 item ids as KPZ-26 asks, and record the identification on both sides — is the correct shape. Disclosure: one of the five papers is PAPER-LE-LEHUNG-LEVIN-ETAL-23, to which this session contributed proofSteps for its Appendix A and Appendix B clusters (PRs #2538 and #2565). Those passes did not create or modify any route, roadmap id or route title, and this review job excludes only RT-AREA-representations-1, but a verifier should say so.

Confirmed, and I recommend raising the severity for one of its two halves. The parent's atlas title is exactly 'Root systems, Weyl groups, and the Cartan-Killing classification' (atlas/roadmaps/tauceti_TauCetiRoadmap_RepresentationTheory_RootSystems.json), and PROTOCOL section 15 requires the form '"<existing roadmap>, Part II: <what it adds>", with the existing roadmap as its first prerequisite'. PAPER-HE-18, PAPER-HE-21, PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-ZHOU-26 and PAPER-ZHU-17 all title the shared candidate 'Root systems, Weyl groups, and the Cartan-Killing classification, Part II: ...', an exact prefix extension. PAPER-LE-LEHUNG-LEVIN-ETAL-23 titles the same id 'Root systems, Part II: dominance, affine orders and admissible pairs', and PAPER-KISIN-ZHOU-25 titles its own id 'Root systems, Part II: integral dominance steps'. Both drop the rest of the parent's title. Severity: the KZ-25 half is presentational and, if finding 2 is applied, disappears with the separate id, so low is right for it. The LLHLM-23 half is not presentational — it gives a second, different title to a roadmap id that four other extractions title correctly, so the atlas would carry one candidate under two names, which is an identity defect of the same kind as finding 2 rather than a wording preference. I recommend recording finding 3 at medium for the LLHLM-23 title specifically, since severity decides whether a fix job is raised, and this half deserves one. The proposed rewrites are exactly right as stated. Disclosure as in finding 2: this session contributed proofSteps to PAPER-LE-LEHUNG-LEVIN-ETAL-23 but neither created nor modified its route titles.
